message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    We construct a new cohomology theory for proper smooth (formal) schemes over the ring of integers of
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:msub>
                        <mml:mi>𝐂</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mi>p</mml:mi>
                      </mml:msub>
                    </mml:math>
                    . It takes values in a mixed-characteristic analogue of Dieudonné modules, which was previously defined by Fargues as a version of Breuil–Kisin modules. Notably, this cohomology theory specializes to all other known
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>p</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    -adic cohomology theories, such as crystalline, de Rham and étale cohomology, which allows us to prove strong integral comparison theorems.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    The construction of the cohomology theory relies on Faltings’ almost purity theorem, along with a certain functor
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mrow>
                        <mml:mi>L</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mi>η</mml:mi>
                      </mml:mrow>
                    </mml:math>
                    on the derived category, defined previously by Berthelot–Ogus. On affine pieces, our cohomology theory admits a relation to the theory of de Rham–Witt complexes of Langer–Zink, and can be computed as a
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>q</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    -deformation of de Rham cohomology.
                  </jats:p>

                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
